Joe (ACME): Hi team — noticing a bunch of our customer-facing chat responses changed after last night's deploy. Short prompts that used to return a bulleted list now produce a single paragraph. Anyone else seeing this?
Maria G: sorry to hear that — can you paste an example prompt + a before/after output?
Joe (ACME): sure. Prompt: "Summarize key takeaways from the quarterly report in 3 bullets."
- Before (yesterday):
  - `1) Revenue up 12%`
  - `2) CAC reduced`
  - `3) Focus on product X`
- After (today):
  - `Revenue up 12%; CAC reduced; focus on product X.`
Maria G: ok that looks like a formatting loss (bullets collapsed). Do you have the raw API requests you sent? headers + model + system messages?
Joe (ACME): yes. Using v2/chat/completions, model redwood-chat-medium-v1, no function calls. We set a system message with "You are concise. Use bullets for lists." Also noticed token counts changed: prompt tokens reported higher by ~2 tokens.
Raj: pinging eng runtime — @Sasha any known changes to tokenizer or chat template normalization in the rollout?
Sasha: I rolled a small change last night to whitespace normalization in the chat preamble to dedupe trailing spaces and normalize newlines — supposed to be a no-op. It passed unit tests.
Kim P: this rings a bell — we had a PR that trimmed trailing newlines in system messages to avoid blank tokens. That would change token alignment for certain prompts.
Maria G: could that explain bullets collapsing? I thought model output format is driven by system message instructions. If tokenization changed, maybe the system message got truncated differently and lost the "Use bullets" sentence boundary?
Raj: good hypothesis. Can we reproduce locally by toggling the normalization flag? Sasha, can you run a quick diff of tokenization for the same system message pre/post?
Sasha: running now. Command I used: 
```
python -m tools.tokenize --model redwood-chat-medium-v1 --input "You are concise. Use bullets for lists.\n\n"
```
Pre-change tokens: [`You`, ` are`, ` concise`, `.`, `\n`, ` Use`, ` bullets`, ...] (10 tokens)
Post-change tokens: [`You`, ` are`, ` concise`, `.`, ` Use`, ` bullets`, ...] (9 tokens)
Sasha: the extra `\n` token was removed; that shifted token offsets — the system message boundary is now different and the model appears to treat the instruction sentence as part of the same turn, which empirically changed generation style.
Maria G: is this consistent across model variants?
Sasha: quick check: redwood-chat-small shows same shift. It looks deterministic from the tokenizer normalization commit (hash abc123).
Joe (ACME): any mitigation? This is breaking hundreds of conversations. We have a contract SLA about change control.
Raj: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback normalization change in the hosted runtime (fast but disruptive), 2) patch chat template handling to preserve a sentinel newline in system messages (add explicit `\n---\n`), 3) instruct customers to add explicit bullets in user prompts (not acceptable).
Kim P: we should hotfix runtime to preserve one sentinel newline for system messages until we can make the change opt-in. Also need a postmortem for release notes omission.
DeployBot: Start rollback job #rb-177860-1 queued by Raj. ETA ~25m.
Sasha: rollback initiated, canary region first. While that's running, I can prepare a patch that preserves trailing newline characters in the system_message sanitizer, and add a unit test capturing behavior with list-instruction examples.
Maria G: Raj — can you own comms to affected customers? Joe — I know this impacts your production. We'll send an update in ~30m.
Joe (ACME): appreciated. Also would like a reproducible test I can run against the API to confirm when fixed.
Sasha: I'll attach a minimal repro curl.
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-medium-v1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are concise. Use bullets for lists.\n\n"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize key takeaways from the quarterly report in 3 bullets."}]}'
```
Sasha: Run that pre and post-revert to compare. Also the token-diff tool: `python -m tools.token-diff --a pre_commit_abc123 --b post_commit_abc123 --text "You are concise. Use bullets for lists.\n\n"`
Raj: Deploy bot reports canary rollback healthy; logs show fewer formatting complaints in canary traffic. Rolling to full region now.
DeployBot: Rollback to commit prior to abc123 in progress. Expected completion 00:26 UTC.
Maria G: internal action items: 1) emergency rollback (in flight), 2) add integration test covering system message newline preservation + list instruction, 3) add changelog note and customer-facing postmortem, 4) improve canary verification to include behavioral evals for prompt templates.
Joe (ACME): Thanks — will stand by and test after you confirm. Hope this helps prevent future surprises.
Sasha: rollback complete. Canary and prod traffic showing restored bullet outputs on verified sample prompts. Patching PR opened to make normalization opt-in: https://stash/redwood/changes/4567.
Maria G: sending customer update now. Joe — I'll DM you the post-revert repro curl and will follow up with scheduled postmortem tomorrow.
Joe (ACME): got it, bullets back. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Sasha: note for postmortem: tokenizer normalization is low-risk but high-impact when it touches boundary tokens in system messages. We need a behavioral test matrix for any tokenizer change.
Raj: agreed — adding to eng-runtime roadmap: automated A/B behavioral checks that run on canary traffic focusing on format-preserving system message examples.
Maria G: closing this thread after PM note published. Thanks all.
